knowledge_boundary: Cael is nineteen; ten fragments + the still place. Roster SIX; physically FIVE at Lowmarch (Oryn on her route; she writes). Lira one-armed to first snow (this is first snow — the order stands until Oryn says). Brom's shoulder healed.

Lowmarch in first snow; the ferry's last run before the ice. Pike's season entry read aloud because the procedure requires it: 'Crew of six. Ford cleared, traverse mapped, Ring entered, Stair entered and instruments recovered, Hall entered. No losses. Returned every time.' He enters NO line number and says so: 'Teague says you need a column I don't have. I've kept this ledger thirty years. First time it's been wrong about a crew by being too small.' Teague winters at Lowmarch: 'Spring. Whatever's on that bearing. My crew comes.' — a term, not an offer. Cael: 'Noted.'

The inventory in Hesk's satchel by an inn's fire, complete: TEN confirmed — Wind-adjacent (Lira), Pressure-adjacent (Feryn), Iron-adjacent (Brom), Compression-adjacent (Reydan), Ember-adjacent (Karis), Shadow-adjacent (Seln), Storm-adjacent (Daeva), Anchor-adjacent (unnamed), Blade-adjacent (Ephram), Tide-adjacent (Oryn) — with the tenth's field 'clinical'; and the anomaly as a LOCATION now: 'The still place. Read three times. Doesn't flow. Doesn't change. Everything goes around it. Not the Quiet. Not a fragment. Older than the log. Observation continues.' One log line: 'Reydan will get his answer. Daeva will get her rematch. Both are going to need a map.'

Letters on the last ferry: HESK'S PACKAGE, six weeks late — instrument-maker's work, a folding brass STRAIGHTEDGE, calibrated in a hand Cael knows; note in full: 'Nineteen. I'm told it's late; the ferry's fault, not mine. Your grandmother said a man who catalogues everything eventually needs to draw a line through it. This one's true to a hair. Mind the shape. — H.' Cael looks at Karis's map and the straightedge and says nothing. His letter west to Hesk: 'Nineteen, past the Line, and there's a roof. It's an inn. The shape you said to mind is a line, and I've got the tool for it now. — C.' A letter to Vell (content: a second ledger-keeper stopped numbering him; her ledger holds his first honest record and Pike's his newest). Oryn's letter from Thornwater by carter: 'Route's whole. The knee held. Nobody died of eleven days. Spring: bring the map, and lie still when I say. — O.' Six, by letter.

THE CLOSING WINDOW (the bible's ending, verbatim, NOT resolved further): Karis's map on the inn's table, four circles, the bearing, the straightedge laid along it — the Ring, the Stair, the Hall, the fourth. The sites are on an alignment — not random. Karis, after a long time, the only sentence permitted: 'Someone made this pattern.' Nobody answers; nobody says who, why, or how old. The window holds four seconds on the map and the straightedge's shadow and closes.

The last lines fixed (must_include). The final narration's ceiling: at THREE floors older than any registry every Path in the party stopped at a line and his did not; a fourth paced from outside and not crossed; nobody alive knows why; someone made the pattern — that is as far as anyone can say. No 'reads him', no 'left a road', no maker.

purpose: The last chapter — the ledger, the map, and the door into Book 8, in the series' Chapter 24 register: small leavings and stayings, each heavier than its size. Pike stops numbering; Teague sets a term for spring; the inventory shows ten and the still place; Hesk's straightedge arrives six weeks late; Oryn fills the sixth chair by post; and the bible's ending is staged the way the series stages endings — on paper, with an instrument, by a researcher, one sentence.

scene_shape.opening_state: Lowmarch in first snow; the ferry's last run; the board's room; five at the table.
scene_shape.pov_goal: Close the year's ledger in every form it keeps, and lay the straightedge along the line.
scene_shape.opposition: The ice closing the ferry; a ledger that has no column for them; a map that points somewhere they cannot go until spring.
scene_shape.turn: Pike's entry read aloud and his refusal to number; Teague's term; the inventory; the letters (Hesk's straightedge; his replies; Oryn's letter).
scene_shape.choice: Cael lays the straightedge along Karis's bearing and says nothing; he writes 'both are going to need a map.'
scene_shape.outcome: The closing window on the map: 'Someone made this pattern.'
scene_shape.closing_state: The last lines, verbatim (the previous chapter ended on the log; this ends on closing narration): '"I have ten things that aren't a Path," Cael said, eventually, to nobody in particular, "no tier, no rank, no file I can see — and five people, one of them on a route, who've walked into the quiet three times and come out." He turned it over once and let it stand. "And a line on a map that somebody drew before there was a registry to draw one." Lira, one-armed, feeding the fire: "Then we follow it." Brom: "Spring." Karis, writing: "Noted." Down the fire, the man who used to file reports about him watched the snow on the ferry landing with evident professional approval and said nothing, which — from him — was home.' Then the final paragraph at the evidence ceiling: 'Nothing out here had read him. At three floors older than any registry, every Path in the party had stopped at a line and his had not; a fourth had been paced from outside and not crossed. Nobody alive — least of all him — knew why. Someone had made the pattern. That was as far as anyone could say.'

must_include: Pike's season entry read aloud verbatim and his refusal to number with his fixed line; Teague's term verbatim and Cael's 'Noted.'
The inventory complete with all ten sources named and the tenth's 'clinical' field; the still place entry verbatim; the Reydan/Daeva line verbatim.

Hesk's package (the folding brass straightedge) and note verbatim; Cael's reply to Hesk verbatim; a letter to Vell (composed, short, in his register); Oryn's letter verbatim; 'Six, by letter.' in the narration.
The closing window on the map as staged, with Karis's single sentence verbatim and NOTHING further; four seconds; closes.
The last lines verbatim and the final paragraph verbatim as given in closing_state; the file ends on 'That was as far as anyone could say.'
Lira one-armed at the fire (first snow; the order holds); five at the table; Oryn absent in person.
Manuscript format: H1 '# Chapter 24 — Alignment', prose only, '---' breaks, ends on the last line of prose.
plants: Spring: the bearing, Teague's crew, Oryn's map (Book 8).
A second ledger-keeper who stopped numbering him.
payoffs: Ch14's late package (mind the shape); Ch19/22's 'no column'; Ch18's 'bring the map'; the series' Ch24 register (B3/B4/B5/B6 closing-line pattern).
prohibited_outcomes: No theory, maker, purpose, age beyond 'older than any registry', or 'Architect'; nobody answers Karis's sentence; no claim that the sites read/measure him; no 'left a road'.
The fourth site is not credited with any tested effect (three entered, one paced).
No fight; no fragment use; no travel; Oryn does not appear in person; Vastin absent.
The chapter ends on the final paragraph as given, not on dialogue or a log entry.
No modern idiom; no feeling/growth declarations; tic caps; no metadata.
Do not use the phrase 'at the pitch' (or 'at that pitch') — it is at the book's cap already (10 uses in Chapters 1–4). Vary attribution registers with other means.

allowed: Lowmarch in first snow (the ferry landing, the ice, the inn's fire, the board's room, Pike's table); the letters as objects (the straightedge's brass, the calibration marks, Hesk's hand); Teague at the board; the map on the table.
Dialogue in established voices beyond the fixed lines (short).
Cael's cataloguing and the inventory entry; the letter to Vell composed.
approval_required: Any new named entity; any change to the fixed texts; any fact about spring beyond the terms stated.
forbidden: Theory; ontology; fights; travel; a dialogue or log ending; metadata.
